items.headline: Combining AI protein design with laboratory evolution improves engineered enzymes
items.excerpt: Broad Institute researchers found that starting laboratory protein evolution from AI-designed, more stable proteins beats starting from natural ones: an AI-designed scaffold gave a protease more room to acquire new mutations. They reprogrammed botulinum-neurotoxin proteases to target ataxin-2, achieving a 79-fold improvement over naturally derived versions. The result suggests generative protein design and directed evolution are complementary rather than competing tools for engineering therapeutic enzymes.

items.headline: Chasing subseasonal forecasts with AI weather-climate emulators
items.excerpt: NSF NCAR researchers are building AI weather-climate emulators such as CAMulator that reproduce complex atmospheric models at roughly 350x lower compute cost, enabling rapid subseasonal (2-8 week) forecasts. Once trained, the emulators generate long simulations in a fraction of the time supercomputer physics models require. The work targets the notoriously hard 2-8 week forecast gap between weather and seasonal climate prediction.

items.headline: Study uncovers multidimensional cognitive effects of generative AI on learning
items.excerpt: A Sungkyunkwan University study finds generative AI improves students' problem-solving efficiency but that high AI-dependency learners score lower on tests while feeling they learned more, a gap the authors call the 'learning illusion.' The work maps multidimensional cognitive effects of leaning on AI during study, distinguishing performance gains from genuine understanding. It has direct implications for how educators and cognitive scientists measure AI's real effect on human learning.

items.headline: Princeton to build AI system to autonomously operate fusion-plasma gyrotrons
items.excerpt: Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory will lead a Genesis Mission project to build an AI system that autonomously operates the gyrotrons used to heat fusion plasmas, alongside virtual simulations of the hardware. The effort is part of a US national initiative to harness AI for fusion-energy scientific discovery. Autonomous control of heating hardware is a step toward AI-managed operation of future fusion reactors.

items.headline: CUNY wins $18.1M to build AI-BIOME, an AI-plus-robotics lab for bio-inspired materials
items.excerpt: CUNY won an $18.1M NSF award to build AI-BIOME, a cloud-programmable national laboratory that pairs AI with robotics to speed the discovery, design and production of bio-inspired materials for uses such as sustainable plastics and drug delivery. It is a closed-loop autonomous-lab approach to materials science, letting AI propose candidates that robots then synthesize and test. The facility is designed to be remotely programmable by researchers across the country.

items.headline: Closed-loop AI framework could shorten clean energy materials development by years
items.excerpt: Tohoku University researchers built an AI-driven framework that fuses materials databases, machine-learning interatomic potentials, large language models, intelligent AI agents and automated experiments into a continuous feedback loop they call the '4th+ paradigm.' Experimental results feed back to refine AI predictions iteratively, dramatically cutting the time needed to discover advanced energy materials. The self-driving-lab approach targets longstanding trial-and-error bottlenecks in materials science.

items.headline: Machine learning accelerates search for longer-lasting materials for solar cells
items.excerpt: UC Davis researchers trained machine-learning models on 137,000 measurements from 10 perovskite compositions to predict how untested compositions would respond to repeated heating. The models found that lower cesium levels let materials recover after thermal stress while higher cesium caused permanent degradation. The approach lets scientists prioritize the candidates most likely to survive real-world operating conditions instead of exhaustive lab trial-and-error.

items.headline: AI's black box problem: discovering physics we don't understand
items.excerpt: AI systems are accelerating physics discovery by finding hidden patterns in massive datasets, from particle detection at CERN to materials innovation at Argonne, yet the opacity of these models means researchers often get accurate results without understanding how the AI reached them. The article asks whether science is entering an era of 'discoveries without comprehension' and what that means for reproducibility and researcher training. It weighs the changing relationship between human physicists and increasingly autonomous AI systems.
